description:
FILED s535a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, resumed s536) from a review probe of perl-tests/scalar.t's moved rows (scratch/s535a/pr/q05.pl q06.pl q08.pl in the s535a worktree; the first probe spelled the variable `$b` by accident).  PRE-EXISTING: main 06a4b8ba and the s535a tree print the same wrong answer.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    my $a = "y";
    package Q;
    print "4 a=$a\n";

perl:              4 a=y
main / s535a:      4 a=        -- SILENT WRONG

Same with `my $b`, with a named sub in the later section reading it (`sub f { "f=$b" }`: perl f=x, PCL f=), and with a FILE-level bare block containing a block-form `package P { }` (q05.pl: `{ my $b = "x"; package P { } print "1 b=$b\n"; }` -> perl `1 b=x`, PCL `1 b=`).  A non-exception name in the same shapes is right on both (q07.pl, `$bb`).

WHY (read, the emission): the exception rename (#296, `_rename_exception_mys` through `_rename_decl_within`) renames the declaration to `$a__excl__0` (a plain `p-let` in the main section) but not the use in the later section, which stays `$a` and reads the proclaimed special `main::$a`; the span pass (port 3, `Pl::Binder::spans`) never sees a spanning binding to promote, because the declaration it would promote is already the renamed token.  (PCL emitted `(p-let (($a__excl__0 :scalar "y" ...)))` then, in `(in-package :Q)`, `main::$a`.)

FIX DIRECTION (not designed): port 4's territory (the exception rename's region = `_rename_decl_within`): either the exception rename's region runs to the binding's real scope end (every later section included) and the span pass then promotes `$a__excl__N` like any spanning lexical, or the span pass runs on the binding before the exception rename and the exception rename spells the promoted cell.  Name-resolution change: the sweep is the gate.  Sibling of #4541 (a file-level `state` across a package, the state prepass's cells).

=== DONE (s536e) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, generation v2-12900; worktree agent-a7512e76832ceacb1, commit 23baa13b).  The span pass promoted `$a` under its OWN name (identity: one declaration file-wide, no package spelling) -- i.e. into the proclaimed special every package declares -- and the exception rename (#296) then moved the declaration off it to `$a__excl__0`, so the later section's `$main::a` read the special.  ONE predicate `Pl/Parser2.pm` `_own_name_cell_ok` (#470's `_file_pkg_global` + `Pl::GlobalPartition::is_exception_global`) is read by the span scalar path, the span container path and the capture promoter: an exception-partition name takes the mangle `$a__file__N` (the exception rename then sees no exception name).  Probed perl -> base c8886b61 -> tree (scratch/s536e/pr/m1*.pl): the reproducer, `my $b` + a named sub, the bare block with `package P { }` (q05), write + back to `package main;`, eval('$a') in the later section, the later section's sort block (perl reads the LEXICAL `$a`: `my $a = 7; package Q; sort { push @seen, $a; ... }` -> 7 7 7) -- tree = perl on all.  A sort with an inconsistent comparator (`sort { $a <=> $b }` with a lexical `$a`) orders differently from perl on base and tree alike: comparator call order, not this.  Side effect: an exception-named CONTAINER spanning a section (`my %ENV`) now REFUSES "spans a package boundary" where it silently read the real %ENV -> #4661.  Guard Pl/t/span-binder-01.t rows 23-26 (23-25 fail on the base; 26 a control).  Emission: perl-tests/each.t, t/comp/fold.t, t/op/each.t (the A/B).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a FILE-level `my $a` / `my $b` (an EXCEPTION-partition name) read in a later top-level `package` section reads the SPECIAL `main::$a` -- the exception rename's `$a__excl__N` stops at the section, the span pass never promotes it (pre-existing; the #4541 sibling)
